question: Indicate which serum biochemical profile is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant:

options.opa: Normal calcium; normal phosphate; normal alkaline phosphatases (FA); normal parathyroid hormone (PTH); 25 OH vitamin D low.
options.opb: Normal calcium; low phosphate; Normal FA; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
options.opc: Low calcium; high phosphate; FA elevated; Normal PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.
options.opd: Normal calcium; normal phosphate; FA elevated; Elevated PTH; 25 OH vitamin D low.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: opc -> suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency -> 80% CHAIN: opc -> low calcium -> possible rickets -> 70% CHAIN: opc -> high phosphate -> suggestive of impaired mineralization in bones -> 60% CHAIN: opc -> elevated alkaline phosphatases (FA) -> indicative of bone turnover -> 50% CHAIN: opc -> normal PTH -> less likely secondary hyperparathyroidism -> 80%
analysis: Rickets due to vitamin D deficiency is characterized by low levels of 25 OH vitamin D. In this case, the serum biochemical profile that is suggestive of rickets due to vitamin D deficiency in a 5-month-old infant is when all parameters are normal except for low 25 OH vitamin D.
